sentences.text: I'm Emily, and in today's episode,
we will talk about a very sensitive topic, funerals.
Funerals are difficult times for everyone,
and it can be challenging to find the right words,
especially in a different language.
In this episode, I will help you learn simple English phrases
that you can use to express sympathy, offer condolences,
and support others in a respectful and kind way.
Today, we will cover key funeral vocabulary,
how to express sympathy and condolences,
what to say to the family of the deceased,
how to respond when someone offers condolences,
common phrases used at a funeral.
Let's begin, key funeral vocabulary.
First, let's learn some important words
that you might hear at a funeral.
People at the funeral, the deceased,
the person who has passed away, mourners,
the people attending the funeral to say goodbye.
Family of the deceased, the close relatives
of the person who passed away, efficient,
the person who leads the funeral service,
a priest, pastor, or funeral director,
Paul Bearers, the people who carry the coffin,
common funeral terms, coffin casket,
the box in which the deceased is placed,
funeral service, the ceremony where people say goodbye,
obituary, a short announcement in newspaper
about the person who passed away,
moment of silence, a short time
when everyone stays quiet to remember the deceased,
wake a gathering where family and friends
remember the person who has died,
cremation when the body is turned into ashes
instead of being buried, grave cemetery,
the place where the body is buried.

Two, how to express sympathy and condolences.
When someone loses a loved one,
it's important to show kindness and support.
Here are some simple phrases to express sympathy.
Short condolence messages.

My deepest condolences to you and your family.
I'm thinking of you during this difficult time.
I'm here for you if you need anything.
You are in my thoughts and prayers.
These simple phrases can help you show your support
in a respectful way.
